# RX Tracker NEXT 4.0.0-next.98

Older eligible audit events, completed import reports, resolved correction groups, page activity and resolved errors can now move to verified database archives. Recent records, unresolved work and operational call references stay active. Initial retention is 30 days per section; daily automatic archiving starts disabled. Existing settings are preserved. Server-level scheduler pauses are visible.

Browse Active/Archived/All, retain complete reports and original CSVs, and download checksummed gzip JSON in numbered pages with event date ranges, navigation and browser progress. Downloading only copies data: the archive remains in PostgreSQL and full database backups. Archiving reduces active-table load, not total database size. Technical log files roll daily and older closed files are verified and compressed; back up logs/archive separately. See packaged docs/HISTORY_ARCHIVING.md.

One audited migration creates archive tables/read-only history views (65 migrations total), without moving rows during installation. Transfers copy, verify and remove active rows in a single transaction with an audit receipt. Migration rollback refuses populated archives. No automatic archive expiration is introduced.

Multer 2.5.0 and Nodemailer 10.2.1 patch current upload/mail-parser advisories. Both executables retain verified Node.js 22.23.4. Existing source, Sequelize/UUID and unchanged Softphone dependency findings remain documented in docs/LOCAL_RELEASE_SECURITY_REVIEW.md.

Verify SHA256SUMS.txt and LOCAL_VALIDATION.json. Install through Project Control option 8 then 15; preserve the paired application/database rollback set, .env and configured RX Actions. Require healthy version 4.0.0-next.98 and review archive settings/history after updating. For emergency recovery use paired rollback (option 16), never an older binary against the migrated live database alone.

Built, database-tested, security-scanned and packaged locally for the exact source commit recorded in LOCAL_VALIDATION.json. Production installation is a separate operator action.
